seed.title: Generative search for single-phase immersion coolants
seed.text: Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, a low dielectric constant and a high flash point. PFAS rules and the end of Novec production are pushing the field towards PFAS-free hydrocarbons and esters. Study whether a generative search over molecules and mixtures finds candidates that beat known commercial single-phase fluids on a cooling figure of merit. More compute buys more candidates checked by GPU molecular dynamics after predictor filtering, and longer simulations per candidate. Score against measured viscosity, thermal conductivity and dielectric data for known fluids held out of training, never against the predictors themselves.
seed.root_question: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
seed.root_link: SAME: a concrete version of the asker's line, kept on discovery and on transport properties (viscosity, thermal conductivity).
seed.compute_open: Candidates checked by GPU molecular dynamics (about 10^2 to 10^4) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether the hit rate against known commercial fluids keeps rising with more candidates, or whether predictor and force-field error caps it.

screen.title: Generative search for single-phase immersion coolants
Force-field error floor for coolant MD: an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark scored against measurement
screen.changes: Changes the comparison it is judged against and what compute buys: instead of a hit rate over novel candidates versus commercial fluids, it is MD-versus-measurement error over an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark that includes commercial coolants. Answers the gap that the Ewen group's MD verification covers only 8 representative molecules with no coolant figure of merit, and measures the ~10% force-field error the original card only assumes.

screen.title: MD-ranked coolant shortlist judged against a self-driving lab's measured property panel
screen.changes: Changes the comparison it is judged against: a self-driving lab's measured viscosity/density/heat-capacity/thermal-conductivity/dielectric panel rather than only held-out literature values for known fluids. Answers the Sinton Lab / FL01 gap (they verify experimentally and by CFD, not with MD) and turns the MD output into a shortlist a named programme can actually test.

screen.title: MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis
screen.changes: Changes the system studied: esters only, inside a synthetically accessible space, instead of esters plus hydrocarbons, with the candidate count anchored to the existing 461-candidate shortlist. Answers the gap that the Org-Mol/SINOPEC team ML-filtered millions of esters but manually picked only two to synthesise and never MD-verified the shortlist; also partially probes whether the best figure of merit still improves from ~100 to ~1000 verified candidates.

frame_best.name: Ewen group (Imperial College London / University of Bath) — MD benchmarking of organic-liquid thermophysical properties
frame_best.step: The GPU molecular-dynamics verification of candidate fluids' viscosity and thermal conductivity — the exact step the card scales to 100/300/1000 candidates. Today the group runs equilibrium MD (EMD) on a handful of representative molecules and benchmarks it against ML predictors for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of C10–C50 organics (lubricants and cooling fluids).

frame_programmes.name: Ewen group (Imperial College London / University of Bath) — MD benchmarking of organic-liquid thermophysical properties
frame_programmes.step: The GPU molecular-dynamics verification of candidate fluids' viscosity and thermal conductivity — the exact step the card scales to 100/300/1000 candidates. Today the group runs equilibrium MD (EMD) on a handful of representative molecules and benchmarks it against ML predictors for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of C10–C50 organics (lubricants and cooling fluids).

frame_programmes.name: Sinton Lab / FL01 (University of Toronto + Acceleration Consortium) — self-driving lab for immersion coolant discovery
frame_programmes.step: The verification/ranking of many candidate coolants — the same pipeline stage the card runs with GPU-MD, which Sinton/FL01 run instead with a wet-lab self-driving lab measuring viscosity, density, heat capacity, thermal conductivity and dielectric constant.

frame_programmes.name: Org-Mol team (SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing + DP Technology + AI for Science Institute)
frame_programmes.step: The post-ML-filter down-selection the card replaces with MD verification: Org-Mol ML-screens millions of esters, filters to a 461-candidate shortlist, then manually picks only two to synthesize and measure — exactly where the card would insert GPU-MD verification of the top 100–1000.

gaps: No programme measures the card's exact quantity: whether the best MD-ranked coolant's cooling FOM keeps improving as the number of MD-verified candidates grows from ~100 to ~1000 (vs. plateauing).

Ewen group's MD verification covers only 8 representative molecules with no immersion-coolant FOM compared against commercial fluids; Sinton/FL01 verify experimentally and via CFD, not with MD; Org-Mol never MD-verified its shortlist.

Activity of the Org-Mol/SINOPEC team is inferred from a July 2025 paper plus multi-year funding; no follow-on release was found by Oct 2026, so its 'active' state is weaker evidence than for the Ewen (Sep 2026 paper) and Sinton/FL01 (Nov 2025 launch, Sep 2026 prototyping) programmes.
